channel.title: Issaquah Dispatch
channel.description: Issaquah news, once a week, from the Issaquah Dispatch.

item.title: The council is expected to adopt the 2027–28 budget on Monday
item.description: The regular meeting is Monday, November 16, at 7 PM in Council Chambers, City Hall South; the city has said final adoption is anticipated that night.

item.title: NW Sammamish Road now stays closed until November 22, longer than the six weeks announced in October
item.description: The road then fully reopens for the holiday, from noon Wednesday, November 25, until Monday morning, November 30.

item.title: The Highlands lights its big tree next Thursday
item.description: The third annual Holiday Tree Lighting runs Thursday, November 19, 5 to 6:30 PM, at Village Green Park, 2550 NE Park Drive, with free hot chocolate, cider and cookies, carolers, and the mayor flipping the switch at 5:15.

item.title: a free repair class and a tool library
item.description: Before you buy a tool for one job, borrow it.

item.title: What Issaquah is doing about traffic and road capacity as new apartments get built
item.description: A reader asked what Issaquah is doing about traffic and road capacity as new apartments get built.

item.title: The council expects to adopt the 2027–28 budget on November 16
item.description: The final budget hearing and the 2027 property tax levy hearing were set for Monday, November 2, at 7 PM in Council Chambers, 135 E. Sunset Way, and the city's calendar listing says adoption follows on November 16.

item.title: Update: Lake Tradition's accessible loop is due for new gravel in early November
item.description: City crews and the Washington Trails Association have fixed drainage and cleared brush on the Bus Trail and part of the Around the Lake Trail, off I-90 exit 20.

item.title: a free day for state parks on November 11
item.description: Wednesday, November 11, is a state free day.

item.title: Whether Issaquah is planning more pool space, Squak Mountain sidewalks, bike lanes or field upgrades at Tibbetts
item.description: A reader asked whether Issaquah is planning more pool space, Squak Mountain sidewalks, bike lanes or field upgrades at Tibbetts.

item.title: The final budget hearing and the 2027 property tax levy hearing are Monday, November 2, at 7 PM
item.description: Any taxpayer can speak for or against the Mayor's proposed 2027–28 budget and next year's revenue sources, property tax included, in Council Chambers, 135 E. Sunset Way, or online by Webex.

item.title: Ballot drop boxes close Tuesday, November 3, at 8 PM
item.description: Issaquah's drop box is at City Hall, 130 E. Sunset Way.

item.title: Lake Tradition's accessible trail loop is getting new gravel, with work done in early November
item.description: City crews and the Washington Trails Association have fixed drainage, cleared brush and pulled out old viewing platforms on the Bus Trail and part of the Around the Lake Trail, off I-90 exit 20.

item.title: Issaquah is the first Washington city with a Charging Smart designation
item.description: The national program rated the city Silver for policies that support electric vehicles and widen access to charging.

item.title: City offices close Wednesday, November 11, for Veterans Day
item.description: VFW Post 3436 holds a service that morning, 11 to 11:45 AM, at the Issaquah Senior Center, 75 NE Creek Way, with a flag ceremony by the Liberty High School Junior ROTC. Service · Closure

item.title: test the smoke alarms when the clocks fall back
item.description: Clocks fall back an hour at 2 AM Sunday, November 1, an easy date to tie to the smoke alarms.

item.title: Who maintains Issaquah's utility poles and overhead wires, and why they aren't kept up better
item.description: A reader asked who maintains Issaquah's utility poles and overhead wires, and why they aren't kept up better.

item.title: Your next chance to comment on the 2027–28 budget is Monday, October 26
item.description: Council takes public comment at its Committee of the Whole, 6:30 PM in Council Chambers, 135 E. Sunset Way.

item.title: Council kept the new 0.01% sales tax local
item.description: King County approved the tax to fund added services for children and families.

item.title: NW Sammamish Road stays closed until mid-November
item.description: WSDOT's utility work just west of Lake Sammamish State Park began October 5; the detour is West Lake Sammamish Parkway SE and I-90.

item.title: The new high school's name moves to a second survey
item.description: After the October 21 ranking night at Pickering Barn, the district's Survey 2 puts a shortlist of names and mascots online in late October or early November.

item.title: Arts grant applications close Tuesday, November 3, at 5 PM
item.description: Project grants are $2,500 or $5,000.

item.title: clear the storm drain before the November rain
item.description: Falling leaves block storm drains in fall and winter, and a blocked drain backs water up into streets and yards.

item.title: PSE's Grand Ridge substation in the Highlands gets its public hearing Wednesday, October 21
item.description: The Development Commission takes testimony at 6:30 PM in Council Chambers, 135 E. Sunset Way, or online by Webex, on the site development permit.

item.title: Council holds a hearing Monday on updated public records fees
item.description: At its 7 PM meeting on October 19, council takes testimony on a new fee schedule for records requests, including increases for police records and body-worn camera redaction.

item.title: The new high school's name gets ranked in person October 21
item.description: Suggestions closed October 14.

item.title: Detached ADUs now have a faster permit path
item.description: Issaquah is the first Washington city to let state-licensed architects self-certify that eligible detached accessory dwelling unit plans meet building code.

item.title: BOO at the Barn is Saturday, October 24
item.description: Pickering Barn runs two sessions: 2 to 4 PM with carnival games and crafts, and 6 to 8 PM with the Haunted Hay Barn, not recommended under age 6.

item.title: free sandbags, October through April
item.description: The city delivers sand and bags at no cost on request from October through April, 7:30 AM to 4 PM on working days, and during flood Phases II to IV: call 425-837-3470.

item.title: Council takes up a 0.01% sales tax tonight, and the rate you pay at the register stays the same
item.description: A special meeting at 6:30 PM Monday, October 12, in Council Chambers, 135 E. Sunset Way, considers an ordinance for children's and family services.

item.title: A $32 million water treatment plant goes to committee Tuesday, on the RV park's land
item.description: The Mobility & Infrastructure Committee meets at 6:30 PM on October 13 for an update on a central plant at the city-owned parcel at 650 1st Avenue NE, next to the Public Works campus.

item.title: NW Sammamish Road stays fully closed west of Lake Sammamish State Park until mid-November
item.description: WSDOT closed it October 5 for about six weeks to move utilities for a fish-passage project.

item.title: The 2027–28 city budget: two chances left to weigh in
item.description: Public comment at the Committee of the Whole on Monday, October 26, at 6:30 PM, and a final public hearing Monday, November 2, at 7 PM, the same night as the 2027 property tax levy hearing.

item.title: Green Issaquah Day, Saturday, October 17
item.description: Volunteers plant native trees and shrubs along the Rainier Trail at Confluence Park, 595 Rainier Boulevard N, and at Park Pointe, both 9 AM to noon; registration is required.

item.title: November 2, not October 31
item.description: The second half of 2026 King County property tax is due Monday, November 2.
